deadline_text_verbatim: Application period -- Irrespective of the applicant's citizenship, once per year: Academc year 2026/27: 2 March to 4 May 2026
limitations: Closed at retrieval (2026-08-22). Verbatim quote retains the source's typo 'Academc'. cycle_year is set to 2027 per the contract's entry-year convention: 'academic year 2026/27' begins in autumn 2026, so the entry year is 2026 for the winter semester -- BUT this same application period also feeds summer semester 2027 admission (see the admission-period rows). The single application period spans two entry points, which the contract's one cycle_year cannot express; 2027 is recorded and this note carries the rest.
researcher_notes: For entrance-exam programmes at Vienna the application period is explicitly citizenship-blind -- the opposite of NTNU and TU Wien, which both stagger by citizenship. Worth recording as a positive fact, not just an absence of a split.

deadline_text_verbatim: Admission Period -- Irrespective of the applicant's citizenship -- Winter semester 2026/27: 13 July to 31 October 2026
limitations: OPEN AT RETRIEVAL. On 2026-08-22 this window is live and closes in ten weeks. One of the very few actionable, currently-open deadlines in this batch.
researcher_notes: Austria separates the APPLICATION period (when you apply, and sit the entrance exam) from the ADMISSION period (when you complete enrolment). Both are hard deadlines and they are months apart. A model with one deadline per programme silently drops whichever it does not store, and the admission period is the one that actually blocks enrolment.

deadline_text_verbatim: Admission Period -- Irrespective of the applicant's citizenship -- Summer semester 2027: 11 January to 31 March 2027
researcher_notes: Future-dated and cycle-bound. Austrian universities admit twice a year, so 'the deadline' for a Vienna programme is at minimum a pair.

requirement_text: My desired degree programme says 'Test doesn't take place.' What does that mean? There is no written test because there are fewer applications for admission than there are study places available this year.
limitations: The entrance exam is CONDITIONAL on oversubscription and is decided per programme per year after applications close. Whether a test exists is not a stable property of the programme.
researcher_notes: A requirement shape the corpus has not met: an aptitude test that may simply not happen. Storing 'entrance exam: required' is wrong in the years it is waived and 'not required' is wrong in the years it is held. The honest representation is conditional, with the condition named.

requirement_text: The application period for the 2026/27 academic year has already passed. You can only be admitted to the course if you submitted your application on time and meet all the admission requirements
researcher_notes: The source states its own currency relative to the calendar, which is why the application-period record above is HISTORICAL while the admission-period records are CURRENT. The page is fresh; the window inside it has closed.

requirement_text: Citizens of an EU/EEA country or Switzerland are exempt from paying the tuition fee for a specified time period. This means: You only have to pay the Students' Union fee during the stipulated degree programme duration plus two tolerance semesters
limitations: The EU/EEA exemption is TIME-LIMITED, not absolute. A bachelor's student pays the tuition fee from the 9th semester onwards (6 stipulated + 2 tolerance). Every other country in this batch treats EU/EEA status as a flat exemption.
researcher_notes: Austria charges its own EU citizens for running late. Storing 'EU/EEA: free' -- correct for Sweden, Denmark, Norway, Finland and Belgium -- is wrong for Austria in exactly the case a student most needs warning about.

requirement_text: Amount EU/EEA/CH -- Students' Union fee: 26.20 Euro; Tuition fee: 363.36 Euro; Total: 389.56 Euro per semester. Amount non-EU/EEA -- Students' Union fee: 26.20 Euro; Tuition fee: 726.72 Euro; Total: 752.92 Euro per semester.
limitations: Per SEMESTER, not per year. The EU/EEA tuition figure applies only once the tolerance period is exhausted; during it, only the 26.20 Students' Union fee is payable.
researcher_notes: Note the scale: EUR 726.72 per semester for a non-EU student at Vienna against EUR 15,000 per year at DTU and EUR 12,000 at Aalto. Austria is roughly an order of magnitude cheaper than its Nordic neighbours for non-EU students, which is a genuine and decision-relevant difference rather than a data error.

requirement_text: Exemption 1: Students from designated developing countries -- The tuition fee is remitted for students with citizenship from one of the following countries during the full duration of their studies. You only pay the Students' Union fee. [45 countries listed, including Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Ethiopia, Nepal, Rwanda, Senegal, Uganda, Yemen, Zambia.]
limitations: The full 45-country list is on the source page; a representative subset is quoted here and the count is stated. Re-read the source before ingesting the list as a lookup table.
researcher_notes: A citizenship-scoped fee remission that is neither EU/EEA nor need-based. Nothing else in this corpus has this shape, and it materially changes affordability for students from 45 specific countries.

requirement_text: Exemption 2: Equal status with EU/EEA citizens -- Submit your application for equal status if you are enrolled in a degree programme and either Belong to a group of persons according to the decree on groups of persons ('Personengruppenverordnung PersGV') or Have a residence permit other than 'Student' (Aufenhaltsbewilligung Student). After your application was approved, the same rules as for students with citizenship from an EU/EEA country or Switzerland apply to you.
limitations: Requires an application with its own deadlines ('Keep the deadlines for your application for equal status in mind!'), which the page does not state on this screen. Not recorded as a deadline because no date was published here.
researcher_notes: 'Equal status' is a legal reclassification that moves a non-EU student onto the EU/EEA fee track. Governed by an Austrian federal decree, not by university policy -- so the decree is the authority and Vienna is restating it.
